summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration for a voting application with multiple services. It defines five application services (redis, postgres database, vote frontend, result display, and worker), plus a visualizer, along with the networks and storage volumes they need to communicate and persist data.

explanations.6: The port is just listed as a number without a mapping, which means the container's port 6379 is only exposed internally to other containers in the docker network, not to the host machine.
explanations.10: This creates two identical copies of the redis service running in parallel, so load can be distributed across them.
explanations.12: When updating the redis service to a new version, docker will update a maximum of 2 replicas at the same time rather than updating all at once.
explanations.20: This line mounts a named volume called 'db-data' into the postgres container's data directory, so the database files persist even if the container stops.
explanations.25: This constraint forces the postgres database to run only on manager nodes in the swarm cluster, typically because managers are more reliable.
explanations.29: Unlike redis, this maps port 5000 on the host machine to port 80 inside the container, so external users can access the voting app.
explanations.32: The vote service won't start until redis is available, preventing errors from trying to connect to a service that doesn't exist yet.
explanations.62: This explicitly sets the deployment mode to 'replicated', meaning multiple copies of this service will run as specified by the replicas count.
explanations.64: This adds a label to identify this service as part of the voting application, useful for organizing and querying containers.
explanations.67: After a restart, docker will wait 10 seconds before attempting to restart the service again, preventing rapid restart loops.
explanations.68: Docker will stop trying to restart the worker if it has already failed 3 times within the window period.
explanations.69: The 'window' is a 2-minute time period during which docker counts restart attempts; if a restart succeeds after this window, the counter resets.
explanations.77: When stopping the visualizer container, docker will wait up to 90 seconds for it to shut down gracefully before forcefully killing it.
explanations.79: This mounts the docker daemon's socket from the host into the visualizer container, allowing it to communicate with docker to fetch cluster information.
